clarifications.already_settled: ADD-02 Q11 answers the question asked: 'Bidders shall design to the figures stated in Volume II. Volume II Clause 4.2 applies.' That is not re-asked. The Authority does not comment on consistency; that the average daily flow (120,000 m³/day, 5,000 m³/h) and the peak hourly flow (7,500 m³/h) are not contradictory (a peaking factor of 1.5) is an engineering reading for the process engineer to confirm. Q11 did not address row 2-6.4 or define dry weather flow (DWF); VOL-II 4.2 itself asks Bidders to raise flow inconsistencies under VOL-I 5.1.
clarifications.gap: 'Dry weather flow' is not defined. If it equals the average daily flow (120,000 m³/day, i.e. 5,000 m³/h), the storm flow to be passed to full treatment (3 x DWF, 15,000 m³/h) is twice the peak hourly design flow of 7,500 m³/h used for the hydraulic profile and the transmission main (VOL-II 4.1, 5.2), so the governing storm design flow is unclear.
clarifications.interim_handling: Proposed interim basis, pending Process engineer (no decision recorded): Design to the stated Table 2-6 figures and carry the more onerous reading (3 x average daily flow, 15,000 m³/h, through inlet works and full treatment) as the hydraulic case, with the 7,500 m³/h case costed as a variant. Record the assumption in the design basis; add no qualification to the Proposal.
clarifications.practical_impact: Sets the hydraulic capacity of the inlet works, treatment streams and channels and possibly of the transmission main and reservoir; a two-fold difference in storm design flow is a major capex and footprint item and bears on meeting Table 2-4 under storm conditions.
clarifications.proposed_question: Volume II, Table 2-6, row 2-6.4, page 4: How is 'dry weather flow' in row 2-6.4 defined, and what storm flow, in m³/h, is to be passed to full treatment and accommodated by the hydraulic profile under Clause 4.1 (page 3), given that three times a dry weather flow equal to the average daily flow in row 2-6.1 (120,000 m³/day) would exceed the peak hourly flow (design) of 7,500 m³/h in row 2-6.2?
